purpose: Keep repository-level paper ownership intact while allowing explicit cross-repository synthesis without accidental absorption or paper-count inflation.

repo_owned_papers.definition: A paper unit whose scientific ownership remains in its home repository even when parts are exported to a larger synthesis.

cross_repo_syntheses.definition: A paper unit that integrates source repositories but owns only the new cross-repository synthesis, not the underlying source results.

modules_and_sources.definition: Reusable scientific components that may support papers but are not counted as separate active papers unless a distinct paper unit is explicitly registered.

future_programmes.definition: Qualified or planned research programmes that are not active paper units until their activation conditions are met.

ownership_rules: one repository may own multiple paper units
one paper may span multiple repositories
export to a synthesis does not transfer theorem or empirical-result ownership unless explicitly recorded
a module or source-only repository is not a failed paper
cross-repository synthesis must identify its new synthesis-level contribution separately from source-owned results

boundary_decision.decision: retain as independent conditional C1; do not absorb into C2 or CED
boundary_decision.headline_claim: mechanistic proximity is not mechanism identification; mechanistic evidence needs an identification axis
primary_surface: row-rank gain iff criterion for an informative new scalar measurement
boundary_decision.submission_strategy: keep parked until C2 editorial outcome; activate if C2 is declined/too broad or if both can proceed under the explicit ownership firewall

governance_test: If a cross-repository paper can no longer state what is new at the synthesis level without re-owning source theorems/results, the integration is invalid and the source-paper boundary must be restored.
